sources.citation: Lahaussois, Aimée. 2009. Koyi Rai: An initial grammatical sketch. Himalayan Linguistics Archive 4: 1-33. DOI 10.5070/H90023670 (eScholarship 5v01m1v6; HAL hal-00447497).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Phonology section 1 (pp. 1-3) covers syllable structure (Ci)(G)V(Cf), initial/final consonants, 6 vowels and 3 diphthongs; no statement on stress or accent anywhere in the 33 pages. Only suprasegmental remark: 'There does not appear to be distinctive vowel length.. It is possible that this reflects an earlier tone distinction, which has now been lost' (p. 3).

sources.citation: Rai, Tara Mani. 2017. Koyee vowels: an acoustic analysis. Gipan 3(2): 136-143. DOI 10.3126/gipan.v3i2.48918.
sources.note: Formant (F1/F2) study of the six basic vowels in k_k frames; nothing on stress, tone or syllable prominence.

sources.citation: Rai, Tara Mani (with Omkareshor Shrestha). 2014. A sociolinguistic survey of Koyee: a Tibeto-Burman language. Report submitted to Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 120 pp.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (dialects, language use, vitality); no phonology and no stress. Its literature review (section 1.3, pp. 13-16) is the fullest bibliography of Koyee work (Regmi 2003a/b, 2006; Rai & Budhathoki 2008; Rai 2010 MA thesis on verb morphology; Rai 2011 NFDIN report) and notes 'very recently a grammar in Koyee (in Nepali).. published' (p. 16).

sources.citation: राई, तारामणि [Rai, Tara Mani]. 2024. किराती भाषामा वर्णव्यवस्था [Alphabet (sound system) in the Kirati languages]. Prajna प्रज्ञा 125(1): 1-22. Kathmandu: Nepal Academy. DOI 10.3126/prajna.v125i1.75263. (In Nepali.)
sources.note: Segmental inventories only, for ~27 Kirati languages. Koyee (Appendix 1 entry 3, sourced to Rai & Budhathoki 2008 and Rai 2015 p. 30): stops/nasals k kh g gh ng, c ch j jh, t th d dh n, p ph b bh m, y r l w s, h (25 symbols in the extracted grid; the summary table p. 6 counts 26) and 12 vowels = a, aa, i, u, e, o each short and long. No tone/suprasegmental row for Koyee or any other language (no तान/टोन/'tone' anywhere in the text, Khaling entry included), so the article is silent on tone; silence in a segment-only comparison is not a 'no tone' statement.

tone.quote: There does not appear to be distinctive vowel length. This point remains to be investigated further. For very common nouns, like nu ‘nose’ and nu ‘name’, attempts seem to be made to differentiate the two, sometimes with length. It is possible that this reflects an earlier tone distinction, which has now been lost.
tone.summary: No tones described; the phonology lists only consonants and vowels. Author suggests an earlier tone distinction (e.g. nu 'nose' vs nu 'name') has been lost; no tone analysis is given.
